hook: Their bill holds three gallons of water.
caption:
Their bill holds three gallons of water.

A pelican's pouch can hold three gallons of water, more than its entire stomach, and they use it not to carry fish home but to strain seawater out before swallowing whatever they caught. Most of the world's eight pelican species nest on isolated islands where predators cannot reach chicks, and those islands are the thing being lost. Rising sea levels are flooding major Gulf Coast nesting grounds, oil spills coat flight feathers and render the birds unable to thermoregulate, and discarded fishing line wraps itself around bills and legs until wounds turn septic; rehabilitation centers in Florida and California now report entanglement as the leading cause of admission. Brown pelicans were nearly wiped out by DDT in the 1960s before the pesticide was banned; they recovered, yet the newer threats are harder to outlaw.
